comparisons.peer_topic: Business Combinations Accounting Policy and Fair Value Allocation
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel allocates purchase prices for acquisitions based on estimated fair values, involving assumptions and judgments for inventory, property, intangible assets, deferred taxes, and goodwill. Adjustments to these values may be recognized during a measurement period of up to one year from the acquisition date, based on comparable market data and management information.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel describe their accounting policy for allocating purchase prices in business combinations based on estimated fair values at the acquisition date. AMD specifies that consideration was allocated to intangible assets, identifiable net assets, and goodwill, while Intel details this process for inventory, property, intangible assets, deferred taxes, and goodwill, noting that adjustments may be recognized during a measurement period of up to one year.

comparisons.peer_topic: Purchase Price Allocation and Goodwill Measurement
comparisons.peer_summary: The company allocates purchase price to tangible/intangible assets and liabilities at fair value, recording the excess as goodwill. These estimates are uncertain and subject to refinement during a measurement period of up to one year, after which any subsequent adjustments are recorded to income.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA outline the methodology for allocating acquisition purchase prices to tangible and intangible assets based on fair value, with excess recorded as goodwill. NVIDIA explicitly states that estimates are subject to refinement during a measurement period of up to one year, a practice mirrored in AMD's disclosure of adjustments for deferred cash compensation and customary closing adjustments in the Pensando acquisition.

sentences.text: On May 26, 2022, the Company completed the acquisition of all issued and outstanding shares of Pensando, a leader in next-generation distributed computing, for a transaction valued at approximately $1.9 billion.
The recorded purchase consideration of $1.7 billion is net of deferred cash compensation requiring future services and other customary closing adjustments.
We allocate the fair value of the purchase price of an acquisition to the tangible assets acquired, liabilities assumed, and intangible assets acquired, based on their estimated fair values.
The excess of the fair value of the purchase price over the fair values of these net tangible and intangible assets acquired is recorded as goodwill.

As a result, during the measurement period of up to one year from the acquisition date, we may record adjustments to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed with the corresponding offset to goodwill.

Upon the measurement period's conclusion or final determination of the fair value of the purchase price of an acquisition, whichever comes first, any subsequent adjustments are recorded to our Consolidated Statements of Income.
